matt: heads-up — running a long-context (32k) int8 run on the staging cluster and seeing weird perf: TTFT improves ~12% vs fp16 but steady-state TPS drops ~18% after ~2k tokens. not expected.

jia: hmm that's sizable. is this prefill or decode slowdown?

matt: it's mostly during decode. prefill is fine, decode throughput degrades as kv cache grows. logs show extra memcpy on the token path.

sofia: do you have a repro command and the perf flame? can you paste the trace id?

matt: repro is here: `./bench --model /models/v2/mixprec_int8 --context 32768 --mode streaming --batch 8 --microbatch 1`
perf trace: perf-bot-> flame://trace/abcd1234 (attached). main hotspot shows `dequantize_and_scale` and `scale_lookup_memcpy`.

devon: quick guess: calibration produced per-channel scales that we kept in CPU memory and we end up memcpy-ing them per token into GPU for the int8 decode kernel. that would explain TTFT win (first token warms) and steady-state drop (per-token overhead).

matt: exact stack snippet from the trace: ```
selected_kernel: attention_qkv_int8_tile
if (!scales_on_gpu) memcpy(scales_gpu, scales_cpu, scale_bytes) // happens every time
launch(dequant_and_attn)
```

jia: why would scales be copied every token? the kernel should cache them in kernel-local constant memory once per request. is the kernel's init gate being hit repeatedly because of microbatching logic?

sofia: check batching heuristics. we recently changed `batching.max_microbatch_size` default -> 1 for streaming, and we also changed the kernel key to include `microbatch_id` in kernel cache key to avoid cross-request reuse. that could invalidate the GPU-resident scale buffer between microbatches.

devon: ack — I reverted that microbatch key change in a local build and saw the memcpy disappear from the trace. but we need a safe fix; we can't re-enable cross-request reuse without reasoning about security.

matt: performance numbers from the experiment: fp16 steady TPS: 3400 tok/s. int8 with bad memcpy: 2780 tok/s. int8 with cached scales (local revert): 3250 tok/s. TTFT for int8 still ~10-12% faster either way.

sofia: calibration side note — we switched to per-tile scale granularity to improve quality. that increases scale table size ~3x. if we keep the table on CPU and copy per token, overhead scales with table size.

jia: potential fixes: 1) persist scale tables on GPU per model/variant and make kernel lookup robust to microbatch/kernel-cache keys; 2) change compile-time kernel to accept device pointer to shared scales (no memcpy); 3) add cheap LRU on device buffers keyed by request id with a small TTL.

devon: option 1 + 2 seems best. we can keep per-request isolation by tying the GPU scale buffer lifetime to the model instance not the request, and ensure we zero-out sensitive metadata (no secret material in scales). ops-bot, any compliance concerns?

ops-bot: scales are derived from model weights and not customer data. storing them on GPU across requests is allowed under current policy. just add audit log for scale table uploads.

matt: good. i'll prototype change 2 first (pass device pointer, avoid memcpy path). also going to add a microbenchmark that exercises long ctx decode with varied scale table sizes.

sofia: one more thing — kernel selection: on some hardware the attention kernel for int8 lacks an optimized KV-eviction-aware path, and we fall back to fp16 attention for very large KV sizes which increases decode cost. check kernel selector logs for `fallback_reason`.

matt: saw `fallback_reason=kv_shard_exceeds_tile` for A100-40GB under 32k context, which matches. we should update kernelselector to prefer int8-blocked-attn if available or break long context into sub-shards with streamed KV.

jia: ok action items: matt prototype device-ptr kernel, sofia update kernel selector heuristics, devon add device-lru buffer with TTL, and I'll add perf regression test in CI that runs 8/16/32k contexts on int8, fp16.

matt: i'll push a draft PR for the kernel arg change and a benchmark script: `bench/longctx_int8_smoke.sh` — posting the branch after I run a couple more tests.

devon: if anyone wants to reproduce locally, here's the minimal script I used: ```bash
python -m bench.longctx --model mixprec_int8 --ctx 32768 --seq_per_request 4000 --gpus 1 --batch 4
```

sofia: thanks — this aligns with what we saw in other clusters. good catch. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note created: perf/regressions/1802504321-scale-table-kv-copy. linked traces: flame://trace/abcd1234, flame://trace/efgh5678

matt: marking as high-priority perf investigation. will update thread with PR link and before/after numbers.
